questions.q: What is the physical difference between a plain BACKUP DATABASE and a BACKUP INCREMENTAL LEVEL 0 DATABASE?
options: None — they back up the same data, but level 0 is registered as a baseline for later level 1 incrementals
Level 0 only backs up half the database
A plain BACKUP DATABASE cannot include archived redo logs
Level 0 backups are always compressed automatically
questions.explain: Level 0 is physically identical to a full backup, but RMAN records it as a usable baseline for incrementals.

questions.q: What does a differential level 1 backup contain?
options: Blocks changed since the most recent level 0 or level 1 backup, whichever is more recent
Blocks changed since the most recent level 0 only, regardless of any level 1s since
Every block in the database, compressed
Only the control file and spfile
questions.explain: Differential is RMAN's default level 1 mode, backing up since the most recent incremental of either level.

questions.q: Why might a team choose cumulative level 1 backups over differential ones despite the extra space and time cost?
options: A restore only ever needs the level 0 plus the single most recent cumulative backup, simplifying recovery
Cumulative backups are always smaller than differential ones
Cumulative backups don't require a level 0 baseline at all
Differential backups aren't supported in RMAN
questions.explain: Cumulative backups trade backup-time cost for restore simplicity — fewer backup pieces to apply.

questions.q: What problem does Block Change Tracking (BCT) solve?
options: Without it, RMAN must scan every block in the database to find what changed; with it, a tracking file lets RMAN go straight to changed blocks
It reduces the size of full backups
It eliminates the need for archived redo logs
It compresses backup sets automatically
questions.explain: BCT makes incremental backups fast by avoiding a full database scan, not just smaller on disk.

questions.q: A team takes a level 0 backup weekly and wants any restore to require applying at most the level 0 plus one more backup set. What should the nightly incrementals be?
options: Cumulative level 1 backups
Differential level 1 backups
Additional level 0 backups every night
Data Pump exports instead of RMAN backups
questions.explain: Cumulative backups always capture changes since the level 0, so only the level 0 plus the latest cumulative are ever needed for restore.
